title: Oracle APEX 26.1: Full CSP Compliance Without unsafe-hashes and unsafe-inline, Dynamic OAuth Scopes for REST Data Sources, Workspace SMTP Controls — Enterprise Security Hardening
summary: Oracle APEX 26.1 delivers a comprehensive set of security and authentication enhancements designed for enterprise deployment requirements. Enterprise APEX applications can now exclude unsafe-inline and unsafe-hashes from CSP headers without browser warnings or functional degradation. Dynamic OAuth Scopes for REST Data Sources: Web Credentials for OAuth2 Client Credentials now support specifying the token scope at invocation time — APEX fetches the token for the required scope without maintaining a separate credential set per scope. New OAuth flows: OAuth2 Password Flow (username + password + optional Client ID/Secret), Refresh Token Support for the Client Credentials flow, Token Authentication Method — choosing how to pass Client ID/Secret to the token server (Basic Auth or request body). REST Data Sources add support for signed assertions and password flows for enterprise IdP integrations. Authorization, Authentication, and REST Source plug-ins: the attribute limit is removed (unlimited attributes) — custom security plug-ins gain full architectural flexibility without workarounds. Workspace-level SMTP Controls: workspace-level management of SMTP credentials for email delivery — governance without modifying APEX instance configuration; protection against unauthorized email sends at the workspace level. Fusion Extensions security improvements: strengthened security layer for Oracle Fusion-extended APEX applications. APEXREST note: APEX 26.1 security hardening is a practical upgrade for enterprise teams with strict CSP and OAuth requirements — CSP without unsafe-hashes closes typical security audit findings in financial, government, and healthcare APEX applications without custom security overlays. Dynamic OAuth Scopes simplify REST integrations with enterprise identity providers and external APIs without increasing credential complexity. For enterprise teams migrating from legacy ERP: APEX 26.1 passes corporate security audits out-of-the-box without custom security plug-ins — significantly reducing compliance overhead for organizations with strict CISO requirements. title: Oracle Deep Data Security Now GA in Oracle AI Database 26ai: Identity-Aware Database-Level Protection for AI Agents — Row/Column Access Control Against Prompt Injection
summary: Oracle announced the general availability of Oracle Deep Data Security — a new security subsystem in Oracle AI Database 26ai that delivers identity-aware, context-aware access control at the database layer for agentic AI applications, analytics, and enterprise workloads. The problem it solves: an AI agent acting on behalf of a user can, through misconfiguration or prompt injection, attempt to access data belonging to other users. Deep Data Security eliminates this through declarative SQL policies enforced in the database engine itself: user identity and execution context are propagated to the database at runtime; policies define what is visible at row, column, or cell level for a given request regardless of who generates the query — application, agent, or raw SQL; an agent cannot access unauthorized data even if it generates an incorrect or malicious SQL statement. Technical architecture: policy execution happens inside Oracle Database — not in middleware or the application layer — eliminating the need to duplicate filtering logic in each application or agent. Availability: included in the current Release Update of Oracle AI Database 26ai for both on-premises and OCI deployments. APEXREST note: Oracle Deep Data Security is a foundational requirement for moving Oracle APEX AI Agents from pilot to production in regulated environments. For enterprises migrating from legacy ERP: database-level authorization enforcement meets data protection requirements for financial and personal data without additional middleware and without trusting the LLM as a security boundary.

title: Red-Teaming Oracle APEX 26.1 AI Agents: First Public Security Analysis 72 Hours After GA — Claude Refused 7 of 10 Attacks on Its Own
summary: Within 72 hours of Oracle APEX 26.1 going GA, an independent researcher published the results of red-team testing the new Oracle APEX AI Agents + Tools capability. title: OCI Cache with Redis (Valkey 8): Oracle Adds JSON Type and ValkeySearch to Managed Cache — New Capabilities for APEX Apps with Vector Similarity Search
summary: Oracle announced GA updates to OCI Cache with Redis: migration to Valkey 8 (open-source Redis 7.2 fork), addition of JSON data type (RedisJSON-compatible API) and ValkeySearch (full-text search + vector similarity search). For Oracle APEX: OCI Cache can now serve as a vector store for RAG (Retrieval-Augmented Generation) scenarios directly in APEX applications without a separate vector database — via REST API with APEX Web Source or the APEX_WEB_SERVICE package. Integration with Oracle AI Database 26ai allows using ValkeySearch as an additional caching layer for frequently queried vector embeddings, reducing load on the primary database and improving AI feature latency in production APEX applications. For teams building AI functionality on APEX: JSON + vector search in managed cache is ready infrastructure for intelligent search without complicating the core infrastructure architecture.
